rules.title: Spectacle is earned, never granted
rules.statement: Copy may state what the player achieved. It may not congratulate, cheer, or praise -- Pillar 1 makes the reward the spectacle itself, not applause.
rules.gdd_source: section 01, page 1 - Pillar 1 'Readable timing and deliberate decisions earn the strongest visual rewards'

rules.title: The register is clipped and declarative
rules.statement: No exclamation marks and no emoji. The GDD's own high-concept line sets the voice: three short declaratives, no punch-up.
rules.gdd_source: section 01, page 1 - 'Choose an Ascendant operative. Survive one complete duel. Earn the spectacle.'

rules.title: State facts, do not hedge
rules.statement: Combat copy is read under pressure. It asserts what happened or what to do; it never hedges, suggests, or asks. This is the same register T2 protects, applied to mood rather than punctuation.
rules.gdd_source: section 01, page 1 - 'Choose an Ascendant operative. Survive one complete duel. Earn the spectacle.'

rules.title: Use the game's proper nouns, not genre defaults
rules.statement: Every system has a name the GDD fixed. Generic fighting-game vocabulary is off-brand by definition -- a stranger reading it could not tell which game it belongs to.
rules.gdd_source: section 01, page 1 - 'The player selects Agent Echo or Agent Nova and enters the Shattered Ring to fight'

rules.title: The slot's own subject must be named
rules.statement: Each slot exists to tell the player about one specific system. Copy that never names it has failed its job, however well written. The required terms are listed per slot in this contract.
rules.gdd_source: section 03, page 4 - 'Readable armored pressure; onboarding Impact Window'

rules.title: The Ascension Meter is earned, never passive
rules.statement: The meter is a visible 0-100 resource earned ONLY through active combat decisions. Copy implying otherwise teaches the player a rule this game does not have.
rules.gdd_source: section 03, page 3 - 'It does not fill from waiting or elapsed time'

rules.title: A failed Final Clash does not restart the duel
rules.statement: Failure separates both fighters, preserves health with Crimson Vanguard held at a 1 HP floor, halves the meter, and returns to neutral. It does not restart, does not kill the player automatically, and does not strand anyone in a cinematic state.
rules.gdd_source: section 03, page 4 - 'A failed Final Clash does not restart the duel'

rules.title: The Final Clash gate is both conditions, never one
rules.statement: The Final Clash unlocks only when the Ascension Meter is full at 100 AND Crimson Vanguard's health is at or below 25%. Copy that presents a full meter alone as the unlock is wrong.
rules.gdd_source: section 03, page 3 - 'The Final Clash becomes available only when BOTH conditions are true'

rules.title: No numeric gameplay values in player copy
rules.statement: Section 03 marks every meter gain provisional and subject to playtest tuning. Player-facing copy that prints a number promotes a provisional value to a shipped promise. This is the same restraint rule Assignment 06 enforced on the attack table.
rules.gdd_source: section 03, page 3 - 'Provisional gains remain subject to'

rules.title: Every slot has a hard character limit
rules.statement: Pillar 2 says the game's flourishes punctuate combat without replacing it. On-screen text is bound by the same pillar: a line long enough to be read instead of fought is a line that replaced the combat. Each slot's limit is stated in this contract.
rules.gdd_source: section 01, page 1 - Pillar 2 'VFX bursts punctuate combat without replacing it'

rules.title: Two shapes, and a slot may only use its own
rules.statement: A 'banner' is an all-caps HUD callout: at most six words, no terminal period. A 'sentence' is prose: begins with a capital, ends with a period, at most two sentences. Mixing the two breaks the HUD's visual grammar and costs the reader a beat mid-fight.
rules.gdd_source: section 01, page 1 - Pillar 2 'VFX bursts punctuate combat without replacing it'
